chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

---

**¶4.** How vast is the potency of the external truths that clothe divine truth? To what degree shall [GAP-1: the external truths that clothe divine truth extend their reach]? That they should flow in with the overwhelming influx of their power and fill this entire stream of understanding in its immensity, as the fullness of all gathered natural knowledge! They have borne surging movements of truth from one boundary of understanding to the other, and extended from one limit of doctrine to the next. The Divine origin from which all these truths issue forth — how infinite must it be? For they flow and flow in every returning state according to the order of Providence!

---

**¶6.** [GAP-2: In the state when] the primordial Divine Human clothed himself in the fundamental substances of truth and good, and established himself firmly against the original opposition that had arisen from falsity, he confronted these dominant and mighty evils. They are beyond reckoning, exceeding in spiritual magnitude any conceivable degree of extension. In the beginning, when he extended spiritual combat against them, he allowed them to receive the fire of self-love and the persuasive force of their own thinking; and thereafter he yielded the external truths to the ruling evils of spiritual death. So those dominant evils absorbed and profaned those truths. Many [GAP-3: truths in abundance] issued forth from the external truths [GAP-4: whence] the streams of doctrine flow. The reception of the dominant evils [GAP-5: swallowed up] those [GAP-6: streams of truth], the aggressive falsities from evil [GAP-7: seized upon them,] strove and brought them forth.

---

**¶7.** There was a fullness of doctrinal streams, like the great flow of understanding [GAP-8: that is perceived], entering into the reception of each of these dominant evils, yet they could never [GAP-9: be brought to satisfy] a single interior will, to their satiation; because the descent into their interior self-love consumes everything with the fire of cupidity and the heat of evil desire. Those dominant evils were like the [GAP-10: insatiable depths] of [GAP-11: the hells]; they were never filled; the influx of truth from above and [GAP-12: the inflowing of good were consumed] throughout all the states of their existence.

---

**¶8.** The degree of that doctrinal stream was expanded to fullness sevenfold, as they flow [GAP-13: through the interior degrees] of the external form of the [GAP-14: containing forms of] truths [GAP-15: in their present state] now.

---

**¶9.** [GAP-16: Behold then, this] is how vast a spiritual combat has been waged, since it has [GAP-17: subdued and confined] these monstrous persuasions from evil, the towering falsities of the will. Behold, they are intertwined, restrained by divine order, and [GAP-18: held fast] throughout every state. They are concealed, not manifest to the understanding of every natural selfhood that dwells in the state of spiritual death [GAP-19: and the realm of the proprium]. These dominant evils [GAP-20: shall at last be] made manifest. The whole of the merely natural selfhood will be vastated and dissipated [GAP-21: in the final judgment]; all of it perishes [GAP-22: and is no more]. They will be overthrown by the wrathful power of their own falsity, which exceeds even the force of divine truth breaking forth in ultimate judgment.

---

**¶11.** [GAP-23: Consider then] the degree and extent of the fundamental substances of truth. [GAP-24: Consider] the spiritual magnitude of the Divine Human who sustained them. [GAP-25: Consider] how infinite is that Divine Being, living in omnipotence, the One whom these truths [GAP-26: surpass in origin, yet who infinitely exceeds] the spiritual magnitude of the primordial Divine Human who [GAP-27: clothed himself in] these external truths of such immensity — and how vast was all that was thereby brought into being.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: How great is the power of the garment of the waters? How far shall [it extend]? That it should enter with the roar of its flood and fill this river Tigris in its vastness like the mighty sea! It has carried waves from river bank to bank, and run from wall to wall. The source from which all these waters burst forth, how great will it be? For they come and come each year at their appointed season!

[At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [from which] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [swallowed] those [waters], the warriors of destruction [seized upon them and] laboured and brought them forth.

There were seven (rivers), like the great river Tigris [that you] see, flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [be sufficient] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [depths] of [the abyss]; they were not emptied; rain and [flood were consumed all] their existent days.
The measure of that river was expanded seven times, as they flow [through the members] of the body of the [garment of] waters [as they are] now.

[Behold, this] is how great a struggle, since it has [subdued and confined] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [fettered] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [and darkness]. These rulers [shall at last be] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [at the end]; all pass away [and are no more]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.

[Consider then] the measure of the elements of the waters. [Consider] the stature of the Man who bore them. [Consider] how great is that god, active in power, the one whom these waters [came from, who is greater] than the stature of the First Man who [assumed] this garment of such size; and how much was made.

fills.explanation: The garment of waters is singular, and "it extend" correctly completes "How far shall it extend?" matching the spiritual reading's sense of external truths extending their reach.
"At the time when" is the standard Kephalaia temporal formula for introducing a mythic event, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "In the state when."
"Many waters poured forth from the garment of waters" maintains the chapter's consistent natural-plane vocabulary; the spiritual reading's "truths in abundance" corresponds to "waters" throughout.
A relative connector is needed between "garment of waters" and "the rivers flow"; the spiritual reading's "whence the streams of doctrine flow" requires this causal link.
"The mouth of the rulers swallowed those waters" fits the established imagery of rulers drinking in and consuming, matching the spiritual reading's "swallowed up."
The spiritual reading's "streams of truth" corresponds to "waters" in the chapter's natural register, continuing the established vocabulary of the garment of waters.
The spiritual reading explicitly places "seized upon them" at this gap; the warriors of destruction seized the waters and then laboured to bring them forth, matching the aggressive falsities' action.
"That you see" is the natural didactic address to the listener, matching the spiritual reading's "that is perceived" and the chapter's rhetorical style of arguing from visible phenomena.
The seven rivers "shall not be sufficient to a single stomach" expresses the insatiability of the rulers, matching the spiritual reading's "be brought to satisfy a single interior will."
The spiritual reading's "insatiable depths" corresponds to "depths" in the natural register, describing the bottomless capacity of the rulers to consume without being filled.
The spiritual reading's "the hells" corresponds to "the abyss" in standard Manichaean/Kephalaia cosmological vocabulary, yielding the natural phrase "depths of the abyss."

The spiritual reading requires a second water-element ("inflowing of good" = flood, paired with rain) plus a verb of consumption; "rain and flood were consumed all their existent days" means the rulers devoured rain and flood throughout their existence without ever being satisfied.
The spiritual reading's "through the interior degrees of the external form" translates to "through the members of the body" in the chapter's corporeal imagery of rivers flowing through a body.
The spiritual reading's "containing forms of truths" corresponds to the chapter's central image "garment of waters"; the body of the garment of waters is the external containing form.
The spiritual reading's "in their present state" naturally renders as "as they are now" in the Kephalaia's expository register, completing the temporal observation.
The spiritual reading's "Behold then, this" marks a transition to the summation of the struggle; "Behold" is standard Kephalaia exclamatory address introducing a revelatory conclusion.
The spiritual reading's "subdued and confined" directly describes the victory over the creatures of destruction; both verbs are natural-register terms that fit the Kephalaia's combat narrative.
In the series "entwined, bound, and fettered," this completes the triadic formula of restraint; the spiritual reading's "held fast" corresponds to "fettered" in the Kephalaia's bondage vocabulary.
"The land of death and darkness" is a standard Manichaean doublet; the spiritual reading's "realm of the proprium" corresponds to "darkness" as the domain opposite the Light.
The spiritual reading's "shall at last be made manifest" requires a future-temporal construction; "shall at last be revealed" marks the eschatological shift from hiddenness to final exposure.
The spiritual reading's "in the final judgment" corresponds to "at the end" in the Kephalaia's eschatological vocabulary, marking the consummation when all flesh is destroyed.
The spiritual reading's "and is no more" is a standard formula of total annihilation; "all pass away and are no more" is the natural-register expression of complete vastation.
The spiritual reading's "Consider then" opens the triadic summary; "Consider" is the appropriate Kephalaia imperative for calling listeners to reason from effect to cause.
Parallel structure with GAP-23 and GAP-25; the spiritual reading repeats "Consider" for the second element of the ascending triad (waters → Man → god).
Third element of the rhetorical triad; the parallel "Consider" structure builds the argument from the measure of waters to the stature of the Man to the greatness of the god.

The spiritual reading indicates the god is both the origin of the waters and greater than the First Man; "whom these waters came from, who is greater than the stature" completes the comparative argument.

"Assumed" is confirmed by both the parallel usage in ¶6 ("the First Man assumed the elements") and the spiritual reading's "clothed himself in," which corresponds exactly to "assumed" as taking on an external garment.
